exposure: BMI category (underweight, normal weight, overweight, obese)
cohort: 2728 pregnant women attending antenatal clinics and private maternity centers in Chennai, South India, from January 2011 to January 2014
finding: Overweight and obese women who gained more weight than recommended during pregnancy had a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, including macrosomia, preterm labor, cesarean section, and preeclampsia.
mod_finding: Normal weight and overweight women who gained less weight than recommended had a protective effect from cesarean section and macrosomia.
